sections.h2: Which Saline County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Saline County splits the work among a treasurer, a chief county assessment office, a board of review and the county clerk and recorder, all in the courthouse at 10 East Poplar Street in Harrisburg. Each office is open on weekdays from eight to four.

  • Treasurer, phone (618) 252-6915: mails the bills, collects payments, and runs the annual tax sale.
  • Assessor, Suite 23, phone (618) 252-0691: keeps a property record card for every parcel and takes exemption applications. Your own record card is free, and other cards cost $0.75 per page.
  • Board of Review: three members appointed by the county board who act as the final authority on assessments, approve homestead exemptions, and hear complaints.
  • County Clerk and Recorder, Suite 17, phone (618) 253-8197: handles redemption of sold taxes and records deeds.

Below the county sit the township assessors. Saline County lists six assessor groupings: Harrisburg Township; East Eldorado, Cottage and Rector; Galatia, Long Branch and Tate; Brushy and Raleigh; Carrier Mills; and Independence, Mountain and Stonefort. For record card or valuation questions the county office is the first call.

sections.h2: When does Saline County send out tax bills?
sections.html:
The treasurer mails one bill a year with two installments, normally due in October and November. Check your bill for the exact dates.

A payment that is not received, or not postmarked, by the due date picks up a 1.5% penalty per month under Illinois law. Taxes unpaid after the second installment are delinquent and subject to publication and the tax sale. Before any sale, the treasurer must send a final notice by certified mail to the owner of record shown in the county tax system, so keep the mailing address on file current if you have moved out of a house you still own.

The tax sale in Saline County is held once a year, usually in January. Buyers bid down the interest rate, starting at 9% and going as low as 0%, and the winner pays the treasurer the taxes plus sale costs.

sections.h2: What happens after Saline County sells unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
The county sells the tax debt, and the owner keeps the right to redeem through the County Clerk for a minimum of two years from the sale date. For homes of one to six units the minimum is 2.5 years, and the buyer may extend any deadline to a maximum of three years.

Delinquent tax steps. Source: Saline County Clerk and Recorder, Delinquent Taxes page.
StepWhat the county says
Second installment missedTaxes become delinquent and go to publication and sale
Annual tax saleHeld in January, bidding from 9% down to 0%
Notice to ownerThe buyer mails a Take Notice within 4.5 months of the sale
Redemption period2.5 years minimum for residential properties of one to six units, 2 years for other property, extendable to 3 years
Court filingBuyer petitions three to six months before the period ends
Tax deedCourt orders the clerk to issue the deed if all requirements are met

Redemption must be paid in one full payment with certified funds: cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order payable to the Saline County Clerk, with the parcel number on it. The clerk can give you an estimate of redemption on request. If later years go unpaid, the buyer may purchase those taxes too and add them to the total with a 12% yearly penalty.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can lower a Saline County bill?
sections.html:
The Saline County assessor lists a general homestead exemption plus several programs for seniors, veterans and disabled owners. Make sure the general exemption appears on the bill for any home you live in.

  • General Homestead: up to $6,000 off assessed value for an owner-occupied home.
  • Senior Citizen Homestead: $5,000 off for owners 65 by December 31 of the tax year. The senior must apply in the office, and a renewal arrives each January.
  • Senior Citizen Assessment Freeze: for owners 65 or older with household income under $65,000, which the county page says rose to $75,000 beginning in 2026. File by July 1 and renew yearly.
  • Homestead Improvement: exempts a new deck, garage, porch or room addition for four years, up to $25,000 of assessed value.
  • Disabled Persons: $2,000 off assessed value for a qualifying owner, with a July 1 annual filing.
  • Returning Veterans: $5,000 off for two years, the year of return and the next.

Disabled veteran exemptions run from $2,500 off to full exemption up to $250,000 of assessed value, depending on the disability rating certified by the VA.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Saline County assessment?
sections.html:
Start by calling the assessor's office with your parcel number, then take a complaint to the Board of Review if the answer does not settle it. The Board reviews assessments, corrects individual ones, and hears complaints on assessment decisions.

Illinois sets a short window for formal complaints. Winnebago and Sangamon counties set it at 30 days after the township assessor's changes are published, so ask the Saline County assessor for the publication date for your township as soon as a change notice arrives. Gather the property record card, the sale price of your home if you bought recently, and sales of similar nearby houses.

A timber or farm parcel follows different valuation rules, and the assessor posts a wooded acreage assessment publication and a farmland valuation page for those owners.

sections.h2: What does the county say about transfers and recording?
sections.html:
The county clerk and recorder records deeds and takes the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, known as MyDEC, which is filed through the state Department of Revenue. The clerk's forms page links to it directly.

Call the recorder's office at (618) 253-8197 before a closing to ask about current recording fees. If your sale involves a sold tax, the redemption is settled through the same office, so have the parcel number ready.

sections.h2: What is Saline County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Saline County is a rural county in southern Illinois, founded in 1847 with Harrisburg as the county seat and largest city. Eldorado and Harrisburg are the two cities, and the villages include Carrier Mills, Galatia, Muddy, Raleigh and Stonefort. U.S. Route 45 links Eldorado, Harrisburg and Carrier Mills, and the land rises from flat lowlands near Eldorado into rolling hills toward the Shawnee National Forest.

The Census Bureau estimates 22,772 residents in July 2025, down from 23,768 in the 2020 census. About 24% are 65 or older. Median household income is $53,117 for 2020 to 2024, and 18% of residents are in poverty.

Owners occupy 72.5% of homes, the middle home value is $94,300, and median gross rent is $726. There were 11,558 housing units in 2025, and the Census lists zero building permits for 2025. Winters in Harrisburg run from lows near 22 degrees in January to highs near 89 in July, with monthly rainfall between 3 and 5 inches.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Saline County house that has unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
Yes, you can sell it, and the first step is to learn whether the tax is still unpaid or already sold. Ask the treasurer about current-year taxes and the county clerk for a redemption estimate on earlier years.

  • Unpaid but not yet sold: the treasurer can give the amount owed with the 1.5% monthly penalty.
  • Sold at the January sale: the clerk's estimate of redemption includes interest and fees.
  • Court petition filed: the final Take Notice lists the last date to redeem and the hearing date, so contact the clerk before that date.

Give those figures to the title company so the payoff is set before closing. A rough house with a long redemption clock may still draw an offer from an investor.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Saline County, Illinois?
faqs.a: The Saline County Treasurer collects it, at 10 East Poplar Street in Harrisburg, phone (618) 252-6915. The treasurer mails one bill a year with two installments. Once taxes are sold at the tax sale, the County Clerk takes over redemption.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty on a Saline County tax bill?
faqs.a: The penalty is 1.5% per month on payments not received or postmarked by the due date. The county says this follows Illinois statute. Taxes still unpaid after the second installment are delinquent and can be sold.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem sold taxes in Saline County?
faqs.a: A one-to-six-unit home has at least 2.5 years from the sale date to redeem, and other property has at least two years. The tax buyer can extend the deadline to a maximum of three years. Call the County Clerk for an estimate of redemption.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for a homestead exemption in Saline County?
faqs.a: Apply at the Saline County assessor's office, Suite 23 at 10 East Poplar Street in Harrisburg, which keeps applications for all exemptions. The senior exemption must be applied for in person. The Board of Review approves or disapproves homestead exemptions.

faqs.q: Which Saline County office files my deed?
faqs.a: File it with the Saline County Clerk and Recorder in Suite 17 of the courthouse at 10 East Poplar Street. The office lists the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, MyDEC, among its forms. Call (618) 253-8197 to confirm fees first.
